key_insight: Human and LLM collaboration can generate experimentally testable synthesis recipes at comparable success rates, and that closed-loop feedback can help uncover new materials such as Ba3PtO5.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests AI-assisted synthesis planning can accelerate materials discovery workflows, especially when paired with human judgment and lab validation.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper candidate materials using both humans and LLMs.
Tested each recipe experimentally in the lab and fed outcomes back into a closed-loop collaboration.
Compared performance across two rounds to assess whether feedback improved synthesis success.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports similar experimental success rates for humans and LLMs across known and unknown materials in two rounds, including discovery of Ba3PtO5 with a new structural prototype.
watch_item: Success drops sharply for unknown materials, so transfer to genuinely new chemistries may remain difficult despite feedback loops.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
